description:

This position is held in NYS Office of Mental Health unit within a medium security correctional facility, under the supervision of Central New York Psychiatric Center (CNYPC). 

1. When RN arrives, gets verbal report from the nurse who worked the satellite unit.
2. Process the MD orders (i.e. input the orders into CNET, print updated MARs, verify new MARs with 2nd RN)
3. Medicate the patients in RCTP OB, RCTP Dorm, Long term care, infirmary, SHU/RRU, Reception unit, and General population incarcerated individuals. (GP)
4. Document medications given, and refused
5. Control and tool count (with 2nd nurse)
6. Stock medication accountability- count stock medications and document on the appropriate form
7. Assess patients brought to the satellite unit, admit to RCTP if needed (documenting RCTP admission form)
8. Document RCTP nursing progress notes.

Current NYS RN License Required
BLS Required

title: Medical Review Officer
description:
Full time position
Monday - Friday 8a - 5p
Schedule hybrid tbd
Approximately 15000 annual reviews 

Every MRO engaged to provide Services must:
  1. Ensure continuous physician licensing and MRO certification as per DOT regulation.
  2. Serve as a completely independent and impartial "gatekeeper” and advocate for the accuracy and integrity of all MTA DOT and NDOT drug testing processes.
  3. Never be or enter into a relationship with a laboratory supporting MTA drug testing processes that would create a conflict of interest with Contractor responsibilities to the MTA.

II.MRO PROCESSING

The MRO is a licensed physician responsible for (1) receiving and reviewing laboratory results generated by an employer's drug testing program, and (2) evaluating donor-provided medical explanations for test results that did not report negative by the employer's drug testing laboratory.
The MRO must be well versed in all requirements specified in Title 49 CFR Part 40 to consistently ensure compliant handling and processing of drug test results reported by the MTA testing laboratory. With respect to MRO responsibilities, Subpart G of Title 49 CFR Part 40 requirements include, but are not limited to:
  1. MRO oversight of staff under direct and personal supervision of the MRO, including all administrative functions such staff may be authorized to perform for the MRO.
  2. MRO retrieval and quality review of negative and non-negative test results from the MTA laboratory and related CCF documentation.
  1. MRO processing of non-negative test results (positive, positive-dilute, negative-dilute, adulterated, substituted, invalid), including:
    • Outreach to the MTA donor to discuss reported test results.
    • Outreach to the MTA DER when assistance with contacting the donor becomes necessary.
    • Determining the legitimacy of medical information provided by the donor to explain a laboratory confirmed positive, dilute, adulterated, substituted, or invalid test result.
    • Verifying a test result without donor contact being made.
    • Verifying and reporting a test result to the MTA DER.
    • Determining and reporting a safety concern to the MTA DER.
    • Cancelling a drug test and promptly reporting to the MTA DER.
    • Processing dilute results as per employer policy.
    • Ordering recollection of a donor specimen requiring direct observation.
    • Informing the donor for whom a testing violation has been verified of the donor's right to request a reconfirmation of the donor's specimen by an alternate laboratory.
    • Ordering reconfirmation testing by an alternate laboratory following donor request.
    • Changing a previously verified test result and informing the Office of Drug & Alcohol Policy & Compliance (ODAPC), as per regulation.
    • Obtaining a memorandum of correction following determination of a correctable flaw.
    • Advising a collector and/or laboratory regarding errors identified and performance issues observed.
    • Consulting/coordinating with the MTA DER, laboratory, or specimen collector when assistance with an issue or correction of a problem is necessary.
    • Sharing electronic or hard copy test result information and related documentation with the MTA DER.

III.MRO MAINTENANCE AND RETENTION OF RECORDS

  1. All electronic and hard copy documentation related to negative test results and cancelled tests must be retained for a minimum of two (2) years.
  2. All electronic and hard copy documentation related to positive and refusal to test results must be retained for a minimum of seven (7) years.
  3. All electronic and hard copy documentation retained must be in a format suitable for easy retrieval, reproduction, and inspection by an auditor or an MTA DER.
  4. All electronic and hard copy documentation associated with an MRO verification, including that provided to or obtained by the MRO, or produced by the MRO, must be maintained securely and in a manner ensuring strict confidentiality of information contained therein at all times.

V.EXPERT WITNESS TESTIMONY

  1. Upon request from the Program Manager, the Contractor shall make available, as necessary, an MRO to provide expert witness testimony regarding the provision of Services and related processes in a judicial and/or administrative hearing where the results of a test and/or MRO verification are at issue.
    • A hearing requiring expert witness testimony will typically be held in the New York City metropolitan area, and will usually be conducted remotely, but may require personal attendance, as deemed necessary by the MTA or the Courts.
    • The MTA shall reimburse the Contractor for any reasonable and verifiable out-of- pocket travel expenses, including meals and hotel, if required for expert witness testimony.
      1. Reimbursement shall only be permitted when the expert witness is required to travel more than 50 miles from home or office to provide testimony.
      2. Reimbursement shall be in accordance with all established MTA travel reimbursement policies.
  2. Upon request from the Program Manager, the Contractor may also be requested to provide documentation consisting of, but not limited to, a description of methods/practices related to Services performed, credentials of MRO and support staff, and related data that demonstrate and support the validity of an MRO verification result reported to the MTA.

VI.OTHER COMPLIANCE, TESTING, AND PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS

The Contractor shall:
  1. Support the MTA's workplace drug testing processes as described herein and will ensure compliance with all applicable regulation and MTA policy.
  2. Ensure every MRO engaged to provide Services will:
    • Maintain uninterrupted licensing and certification, as specified by DOT regulation.
    • Never be or enter into a relationship with a laboratory supporting MTA drug testing processes that would create a conflict of interest with Contractor responsibilities to the MTA.
  3. Upon request, provide the Program Manager with evidence of all necessary MRO licensing and certification as per regulation.
  1. As per DOT regulation, ensure personal MRO quality review of at least 5% of all DOT CCFs reviewed by MRO staff on a quarterly basis, including review of negative results and those requiring corrective action (but no more than 500 reviews per calendar quarter).
  2. Upon request from the Program Manager, the Contractor shall provide a raw data report in a .csv or .xls format across a time period specified by the Program Manager related to the provision of Services to the MTA, inclusive of MTA laboratory account, test result and testing category (e.g., pre-employment, random, post-accident, reasonable suspicion, etc.) reported by the MTA laboratory, MRO verification, and other data deemed necessary by the Program Manager.
  3. Meet key performance targets as specified in a Service Level Agreement for Services performed under the contact.

VII.CLIENT SUPPORT

The Contractor shall provide telephone and email support between the hours of 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM EST, Monday through Friday. Qualified professional/technical representatives will be available to resolve issues or problems related to the provision of Services, including but not limited to MRO verification status, electronic transmission of test results and related documentation to the MTA DER, invoice/contract support, as well as federal/state regulatory developments relevant to the MTA.
As needed, the Contractor will also:
  1. Take prompt action to escalate matters reported by the Program Manager as being of high urgency.
  2. Provide access to a certified MRO for consultation between the hours of 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM EST, Monday through Friday.
Salary commensurate with scope of work job experience
Proper footwear required to perform tasks in a safe manner.
Perform other reasonably related duties as required.
